newsitem.title: CHINA: China Peugeot carmaker to seek new foreign partner.
newsitem.headline: China Peugeot carmaker to seek new foreign partner.

text.p: The Sino-French car joint venture Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile will break up and be reformed with a new foreign partner later this year, a Chinese official said on Tuesday.

"The Chinese and French sides are better off separated than together," an official of the Guangdong provincial automobile industry office said by telephone in an indication Peugeot was pulling out of the venture.
The joint venture would change its name, the official told Reuters from Guangzhou, capital of southern Guangdong province.
The Press Digest newspaper, in an edition seen in Beijing on Tuesday, said Peugeot had "basically agreed" to pull out.
Peugeot officials reached by telephone in Guangzhou declined to comment.
French media has reported that the project was on the brink of failure.

PSA Peugeot Citroen Chairman Jacques Calvet said in Paris last month the company aimed to group its production in China at the Citroen plant in the central city of Wuhan. Peugeot has cited difficulties with monetary tightening in China and disagreements with its Chinese partner over the models in production.

More than 10 foreign carmakers have expressed an interest in taking a stake in Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile, including South Korea's Hyundai Motor Co, Japan's Honda Motor Co Ltd, and Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp of the United States, the official said.
Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile is 30 percent owned by Peugeot and has produced only 100,000 cars since it went into production in 1986.
The joint venture stopped production several months ago. The Press Digest said the company lost 300 million yuan ($36.1 million) last year.
Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile has said it planned to expand with an investment of 7.0-8.0 billion yuan in the next three years.
